paths.naming: Controller bindings are JSON under `input`: `input_profiles` contains 19-element binding arrays using Key, ControllerButton, ControllerAxis, or raw JoystickButton/JoystickHat/JoystickAxis objects; `input_profile_binding` selects players
paths.path: ~/.config/gopher64/config.json (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gopher64/); portable.txt next to the executable switches config to <exe dir>/portable_data/config. Config is a single JSON document written by serde_json (pretty). Controller configuration lives inside it under the "input" key: "input_profiles" is a map of profile name -> {"inputs": [[binding, binding] x 19 logical N64 inputs (dpad, start, Z, A/B/C-buttons/triggers, analog axis, hotkey)], "dinput": bool, "deadzone": int} where each binding is null or {"Key":{"id":N}} (keyboard), {"ControllerButton":{"id":N}}, {"ControllerAxis":{"id","axis","initial_state"}} (SDL3 gamepad), or {"JoystickButton"}/{"JoystickHat"}/{"JoystickAxis"} (raw joystick); "input_profile_binding" [4] names the profile per player port (a "default" profile with SDL3 keyboard + Xbox-style gamepad defaults is created on first run and cannot be deleted); "controller_assignment" [4], "controller_enabled" [4], "transfer_pak" [4], "gb_rom_path"/"gb_ram_path" [4]. cheats.json and retroachievements.json sit beside config.json

linux.notes: Flatpak io.github.gopher64.gopher64 redirects these directories into ~/.var/app/io.github.gopher64.gopher64/ and needs --filesystem=host:ro to open ROMs outside the sandbox (README). The native Linux controller adapter uses a private XDG_CONFIG_HOME but deliberately leaves XDG_DATA_HOME untouched, so native saves/states stay in the directories above. Portable mode overrides XDG roots and is explicitly rejected by the adapter.
